title: Slack vs Discord (2026): Team Chat or Community Platform?
description: Compare Slack and Discord for team communication, channels, voice conversations, integrations, administration, and community workflows. The right fit depends on whether you need workplace collaboration or a community-oriented server.

features.name: Primary context
features.tool2: Community servers, group chat, and voice communities
features.tool1Detail: Slack is designed around workplace conversations and connections to business tools. Review current plans and feature availability: https://slack.com/pricing
features.tool2Detail: Discord is organized around servers and communities with text and voice channels. Review its current feature and subscription options: https://discord.com

features.name: Channel organization
features.tool1: Channels organized around teams, projects, and topics
features.tool2: Servers containing topic-based text and voice channels
features.tool1Detail: Test channel discovery, membership, private conversations, retention, and how work discussions connect to your team's process.
features.tool2Detail: Test server structure, role permissions, channel access, moderation, and how new members discover the right conversations.

features.name: Voice and live conversations
features.tool1: Huddles and workplace calls, depending on plan and setup
features.tool2: Voice channels and live community conversations
features.tool1Detail: Check the current plan and client support for the meeting and huddle workflows your team requires: https://slack.com/pricing
features.tool2Detail: Run a realistic voice session with your typical group size and check current features, moderation, and access controls: https://support.discord.com

features.name: Business integrations and automation
features.tool1: Business app integrations and workflow connections
features.tool1Detail: List the business systems you need and test each required integration in your intended plan. Start with Slack's official app directory: https://slack.com/apps
features.tool2Detail: Check whether the required bot or app is maintained, permitted by your server policy, and able to access only the data it needs: https://discord.com/developers/docs/intro

features.name: Administration and access
features.tool2: Server roles, channel permissions, and moderation controls
features.tool1Detail: Verify member lifecycle, guest access, admin roles, retention, and any enterprise controls required by your organization: https://slack.com/trust
features.tool2Detail: Verify roles, invitations, moderation, audit needs, and access removal using a test server before relying on it for sensitive work: https://discord.com/safety

features.name: Search and information retrieval
features.tool1: Search across workplace conversations and connected work
features.tool2: Search across server conversations and community channels
features.tool1Detail: Test finding old decisions, files, and project discussions under the retention and plan settings you expect to use.
features.tool2Detail: Test finding older messages and pinned resources in a representative server; check whether the information structure remains manageable as the community grows.

features.name: Security and compliance needs
features.tool1: Business security and compliance options vary by plan
features.tool2: Security and moderation features aimed at server and community use
features.tool1Detail: Do not infer compliance from a feature list. Review current security documentation and contract terms for your requirements: https://slack.com/trust
features.tool2Detail: Review current security documentation and policies, and confirm whether Discord's available controls meet your organization's obligations: https://discord.com/safety

features.name: Pricing and limits
features.tool1: Free and paid workplace plans; limits depend on current terms
features.tool2: Free access with optional paid subscriptions and server-specific options
features.tool1Detail: Compare seats, message access, integrations, administration, and billing term on the official pricing page: https://slack.com/pricing
features.tool2Detail: Check the current subscription and server feature options directly; do not assume paid consumer features are equivalent to workplace administration: https://discord.com

features.name: Adoption and fit
features.tool1: Often a natural fit when work conversations connect to business processes
features.tool2: Often a natural fit when voice, community participation, and server roles are central
features.tool1Detail: Ask representatives from each role to test notifications, channel organization, search, and the business integrations they use daily.
features.tool2Detail: Test onboarding, moderation, voice participation, role management, and whether the community structure fits your team or audience.

verdict: Slack and Discord overlap in messaging and voice, but they are built around different operating contexts. Slack is a reasonable starting point when conversations need to connect to workplace tools, project discussions, and business administration. Discord is a reasonable starting point when server communities, voice channels, and community participation are central. Neither is a verified universal winner, and a community server is not automatically a substitute for workplace governance. Test access control, search, retention, integrations, moderation, and the exact plan limits you need. Confirm current security terms and pricing directly with each vendor before moving internal or sensitive conversations.

faqs.question: Is Slack or Discord better for a work team?
faqs.answer: Slack is usually the more natural starting point when workplace conversations must connect to business tools and company administration. Discord can fit teams whose collaboration is centered on voice channels or an existing community server. Verify your access, retention, and security requirements before choosing.

faqs.question: Can Discord replace Slack?
faqs.answer: It may work for a team with straightforward chat and voice needs, but do not assume it provides equivalent workplace administration, retention, compliance, or business integrations. Test those requirements against current vendor documentation before migrating.

faqs.question: Can Slack replace Discord for a community?
faqs.answer: Slack can support group conversations, but Discord's server and voice-channel model may be a better fit for communities where live voice, roles, moderation, and public participation are central. Test onboarding and moderation with representative members.

faqs.question: Which is better for voice chat?
faqs.answer: Discord is built around persistent voice channels and community participation, while Slack offers workplace huddles and calls. Compare the current features, access controls, client support, and plan limits for the group size you expect.

faqs.question: Which has better integrations?
faqs.answer: The answer depends on the systems and bots you need. Slack has a business app directory, while Discord supports apps and bots for server workflows. Verify that each required integration is maintained and supports your exact use case.

faqs.question: Which one costs less?
faqs.answer: Do not compare headline prices alone. Check the current plans, seat counts, billing terms, administration needs, and any paid features required by your workflow on the official vendor sites.

faqs.question: Is Discord appropriate for sensitive company information?
faqs.answer: Make the decision against your organization's security, retention, administration, and compliance requirements. Review current policies and contractual terms directly with Discord and your security team; do not infer suitability from the availability of private channels alone.

faqs.question: What should we test before switching?
faqs.answer: Test channel organization, search, access removal, retention, integrations, notifications, voice quality, moderation, and exports. Run a small pilot with real workflows and verify every required capability in the intended plan.
